```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Wu_2026_contezolid")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01033-25>
* Supplemental material (Fig. S1 to S3, Table S1): available from the article
  page.

Wu 2026 report the clinical efficacy, safety and lung penetration of oral
contezolid in adults with pneumonia. The population PK model was fitted in
NONMEM 7.5.6 (FOCE with interaction) to plasma and urea-corrected epithelial
lining fluid (ELF) concentrations. The structural model, the covariate
equations and the differential equations are given only in the supplement
(Fig. S1 and the equation under "Supplementary Details on Population PK
Analysis (Results)"); the estimates are in supplement Table S1.

# Population

Fifteen hospitalised Chinese adults with clinically confirmed or suspected
gram-positive pneumonia (14 community-acquired, 1 hospital-acquired) at
Zhongshan Hospital (Fudan University) and Shanghai First People's Hospital
(Table 1): 9 men and 6 women, age 36-73 years (median 58), weight 47-105 kg
(median 65), BMI 17.3-29.3 kg/m^2, eGFR 79-117 mL/min. All received contezolid
tablets 800 mg every 12 h for 7 to 14 days. Serial plasma samples were taken
after the fifth or sixth dose; 13 patients had bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) at
2, 4 or 6 h after the fifth or sixth dose, and 11 contributed an evaluable ELF
concentration. The 13 BAL patients took their doses fasted (required before
bronchoscopy) and the 2 others after a meal. The model was built on 75 plasma
and 11 ELF concentrations.

The same information is stored in the model:

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: depot -> central <-> ELF, first-order absorption with lag | -- | Supplement Fig. S1 and its differential equations; main text Methods "Population PK analysis" |
| `lka` (Ka at the albumin reference) | 0.48 1/h | Table S1 `Ka`; supplement Results equation |
| Albumin effect on Ka, `(ALB/0.93)^8.02` | not encoded | Table S1 `Ka(ALB)` = 8.02; see Assumptions |
| `ltlag` | 0.083 h | Table S1 `TLAG` |
| `lcl` | 9.42 L/h | Table S1 `CL`; equation `CL (L/h) = 9.42` |
| `lvc` | 13.11 L | Table S1 `Vc` |
| `lvelf` | 12.82 L | Table S1 `VELF` |
| `lk_central_elf` | 0.99 1/h | Table S1 `KCELF` |
| `lk_elf_central` | 2.99 1/h | Table S1 `KELFC` |
| `lfdepot` (fasted bioavailability) | 0.557 | Supplement Results equation `BIO = 0.557 x 1.83^FASTING x exp(eta3 + kappa)` |
| `e_fed_fdepot` | 1.83 | Table S1 `BIO(FASTING)` |
| `etalka` | 0.839 | Table S1 omega2 Ka |
| `etalk_central_elf` | 0.47 | Table S1 omega2 KCELF |
| `etalfdepot` | 0 (fixed) | eta3 appears in the BIO equation; no Table S1 row |
| `etaiov_fdepot_1`, `etaiov_fdepot_2` | 0.066 | Table S1 pi2 BIO (inter-occasion) |
| `propSd_zhongshan` | sqrt(0.26) = 0.510 | Table S1 sigma2 Zhongshan_Plasma |
| `propSd_firsthosp` | sqrt(0.13) = 0.361 | Table S1 sigma2 First_hospital_Plasma |
| `propSd_Celf` | sqrt(1e-6) = 0.001 | Table S1 sigma2 Zhongshan_ELF |
| Site-stratified proportional error | -- | Supplement Methods residual-error equations |
| `Cc = central / vc`, `Celf = elf / velf` | -- | Supplement differential equations, with bioavailability applied once (see Assumptions) |

# Virtual cohort and simulation

The simulated patients take 800 mg every 12 h for five days (10 doses) and are
summarised over the last dosing interval (108-120 h), by which time the
model is at steady state (its slowest disposition half-life is under 1.5 h).
Each patient has a single sampled occasion (`OCC = 1`), as in the study, so
the inter-occasion term varies bioavailability once per patient. Half the
patients are assigned to each recruiting hospital; the site changes only the
residual error, which the summaries below do not use (they use the individual
prediction `Cc`). The main cohort is fasted, like the 13 patients who
contributed both plasma and ELF.

```{r events}
make_events <- function(n, fed, id_offset = 0) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, 108, by = 12)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 800, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    id = ids,
    time = c(seq(0, 104, by = 4), seq(108, 120, by = 0.25))
  ) |>
    # Observation rows sit on the central ODE state with dvid = 1 (the first
    # endpoint, Cc); rxode2 returns both Cc and Celf as columns on every row.
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      FED = fed,
      OCC = 1L,
      STUDY_SHANGHAI_FIRST = as.integer(id %% 2 == 0)
    )
}

n_per_arm <- 200
ev_fasted <- make_events(n_per_arm, fed = 0L)
ev_fed <- make_events(n_per_arm, fed = 1L, id_offset = n_per_arm)
```

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261121)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = dplyr::bind_rows(ev_fasted, ev_fed),
  keep = c("FED"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(state = ifelse(FED == 1, "Fed", "Fasted"))

ss <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 108) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 108)
```

# Typical-value profile (replicates Figure 3)

Figure 3 of Wu 2026 shows the model-simulated total plasma, ELF and free
plasma (10% of total, from the literature protein binding of 90%) profiles.
The typical fasted patient is shown below with the observed means at 2, 4 and
6 h after the dose from Table 4 (the patients with an evaluable ELF sample)
overlaid.

```{r typical}
ev_typ <- make_events(1, fed = 0L)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = ev_typ,
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 108) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 108)

typ_long <- typ |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    tad,
    `Total plasma` = Cc,
    ELF = Celf,
    `Free plasma` = 0.1 * Cc
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-tad, names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc")

table4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tad, ~matrix,        ~conc,
  2,    "Total plasma", 6.15,
  4,    "Total plasma", 6.31,
  6,    "Total plasma", 5.51,
  2,    "ELF",          3.39,
  4,    "ELF",          2.42,
  6,    "ELF",          1.76,
  2,    "Free plasma",  0.62,
  4,    "Free plasma",  0.63,
  6,    "Free plasma",  0.55
)

ggplot(typ_long, aes(tad, conc, colour = matrix)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = table4, size = 2.5, shape = 17) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 12, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)",
    y = "Contezolid concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Lines: typical fasted patient. Triangles: observed means, Wu 2026 Table 4.",
      "Replicates Figure 3 of Wu 2026."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Stochastic profiles

```{r vpc}
vpc <- ss |>
  dplyr::select(id, state, tad, `Total plasma` = Cc, ELF = Celf) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`Total plasma`, ELF), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::group_by(state, matrix, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05),
    p50 = median(conc),
    p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

obs4 <- table4 |>
  dplyr::filter(matrix != "Free plasma") |>
  dplyr::mutate(state = "Fasted")

ggplot(vpc, aes(tad, p50, colour = matrix, fill = matrix)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = obs4, aes(y = conc), shape = 17, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~state) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)",
    y = "Contezolid concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Median and 90% interval of 200 simulated patients per state; triangles: Table 4 observed means (fasted)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Deterministic checks

At steady state the typical plasma AUC over a dosing interval is
`Dose x F / CL`, and the ELF-to-plasma AUC ratio is
`(k_central_elf / k_elf_central) x (Vc / VELF)`, independent of absorption.
Both are checked against the typical-value solve.

```{r deterministic}
auc_trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
typ_fine <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = make_events(1, fed = 0L) |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(
      id = 1, time = seq(108, 120, by = 0.01), amt = NA_real_,
      evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L, FED = 0L, OCC = 1L, STUDY_SHANGHAI_FIRST = 0L
    )),
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
auc_plasma_typ <- auc_trap(typ_fine$time, typ_fine$Cc)
auc_elf_typ <- auc_trap(typ_fine$time, typ_fine$Celf)
auc_closed <- 800 * 0.557 / 9.42
ratio_closed <- (0.99 / 2.99) * (13.11 / 12.82)

data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Plasma AUC0-12,ss (mg.h/L)", "ELF/plasma AUC ratio"),
  Solve = signif(c(auc_plasma_typ, auc_elf_typ / auc_plasma_typ), 4),
  `Closed form` = signif(c(auc_closed, ratio_closed), 4),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical fasted patient at steady state.")

# Both sides use the same parameters, so the difference is numerical error
# (trapezoid on a 0.01-h grid plus the 10 doses' residual approach to steady
# state, together well under 0.1%). A mis-transcribed CL, F, volume or rate
# constant moves these by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_plasma_typ / auc_closed - 1) < 0.002,
  abs((auc_elf_typ / auc_plasma_typ) / ratio_closed - 1) < 0.002
)
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- ss |>
  dplyr::select(id, tad, state, Cc, Celf) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Celf), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    treatment = paste(state, ifelse(matrix == "Cc", "plasma", "ELF"), sep = " - ")
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time = tad, conc, treatment)

dose_df <- conc_df |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 800)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 12,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res), caption = "Steady-state NCA over the last dosing interval (200 simulated patients per state).")
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table 3 of Wu 2026 reports the mean non-compartmental plasma parameters from
the observed (13 fasted, 2 fed) patients. Table 4 reports the model-based
ELF AUC0-12,ss of the patients with an ELF sample (median 22.42 mg.h/L).
The simulated column is the median of the fasted cohort.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,         ~cmax, ~cmin, ~tmax, ~auclast,
  "Fasted - plasma",   9.55,  1.28,  2,     56.06,
  "Fasted - ELF",      NA,    NA,    NA,    22.42
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L", tmax = "h", auclast = "mg.h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated (median of 200 fasted patients) vs. published",
  "(Table 3 NCA means for plasma; Table 4 model-based median for ELF).",
  "* differs from the reference by more than 20%."
))
```

```{r ratio}
ratio <- conc_df |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^Fasted", treatment)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = auc_trap(time, conc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(matrix = ifelse(grepl("ELF", treatment), "elf", "plasma")) |>
  dplyr::select(-treatment) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = matrix, values_from = auc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = elf / plasma)

data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Median", "Mean"),
  Simulated = signif(c(median(ratio$ratio), mean(ratio$ratio)), 3),
  `Wu 2026 Table 4` = c(0.35, 0.45),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "ELF-to-total-plasma AUC0-12,ss ratio, fasted patients.")

# The ratio depends only on k_central_elf (which carries IIV) and fixed
# volumes, so its median is the typical 0.339 up to sampling error (log-scale
# SD 0.69, n = 200: standard error of the median about 6%). 15% is about 2.5
# of those standard errors and still fails on a mis-transcribed rate constant
# or volume.
stopifnot(abs(median(ratio$ratio) / 0.35 - 1) < 0.15)
```

The simulated median plasma AUC0-12,ss and Cmax of the fasted cohort are
close to the observed NCA means, and Tmax matches. The simulated Cmin is far
below the observed mean of 1.28 mg/L; see Assumptions and deviations. The
simulated ELF AUC is below the paper's model-based median by about the same
proportion as the simulated plasma AUC is below the paper's model-based plasma
median (61.05 mg.h/L, Table 4), so the shortfall is in plasma exposure, not in
lung penetration. The
median ELF-to-plasma AUC ratio reproduces the paper's median of 0.35, and the
simulated mean ratio, raised by the between-subject variability on the
central-to-ELF rate constant, is close to the paper's mean of 0.45.

# Probability of target attainment (replicates Figure 4)

Wu 2026 computed the probability that the free plasma AUC0-24 at steady state
divided by the MIC reaches 2.3, with an unbound fraction of 10%, from 5000
simulated patients on 800 mg every 12 h. Their PTA was 92.5% at an MIC of
4 mg/L and about 13% at 8 mg/L (values read from Figure 4). The simulated
fasted and fed cohorts are shown below.

```{r pta}
fauc24 <- conc_df |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("plasma", treatment)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(fauc24 = 0.1 * 2 * auc_trap(time, conc), .groups = "drop")

mics <- 2^seq(-4, 5)
pta <- tidyr::expand_grid(fauc24, MIC = mics) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, MIC) |>
  dplyr::summarise(PTA = 100 * mean(fauc24 / MIC >= 2.3), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(source = sub(" - plasma", "", treatment)) |>
  dplyr::select(source, MIC, PTA)

pta_paper <- tibble::tibble(
  source = "Wu 2026 Figure 4",
  MIC = mics,
  PTA = c(100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 99.7, 92.5, 13, 0, 0)
)

ggplot(dplyr::bind_rows(pta, pta_paper), aes(MIC, PTA, colour = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics, labels = format(mics, drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Target fAUC0-24/MIC >= 2.3, unbound fraction 0.1. Replicates Figure 4 of Wu 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

pta_wide <- pta |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = PTA) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(pta_paper, MIC, `Wu 2026 Figure 4` = PTA), by = "MIC")
pta_at <- function(src, mic) {
  v <- pta_wide[[src]][pta_wide$MIC == mic]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique PTA for ", src, " at MIC ", mic)
  v
}
pta_wide |>
  dplyr::mutate(MIC = vapply(MIC, format, character(1), drop0trailing = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::rename(`MIC (mg/L)` = MIC) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "PTA (%) by MIC.")
```

The published curve lies between the simulated fasted and fed curves. At an
MIC of 4 mg/L the simulated fasted PTA is `r round(pta_at("Fasted", 4))`%
(published 92.5%) and the fed PTA `r round(pta_at("Fed", 4))`%; at 8 mg/L the
fasted PTA is `r round(pta_at("Fasted", 8))`% and the fed
`r round(pta_at("Fed", 8))`% (published 13%). The published curve implies a
median steady-state plasma AUC0-12 near 68 mg.h/L with a log-scale spread of
about 0.27 (the spread matches the model's inter-occasion variability on
bioavailability, 0.066 on the variance scale). The paper does not state the
food state or covariate values of its simulated patients, so this is not a
validation target; see Assumptions and deviations.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Bioavailability applied once.** The supplement divides CL, Vc and VELF by
  BIO (`CL_CORR = CL/BIO` and so on) and also sets the initial depot amount to
  `Dose x BIO`. Read literally, concentrations would scale with BIO squared
  (typical fasted AUC0-12,ss about 26 mg.h/L, half the observed NCA value of
  56). The model applies BIO once, through `f(depot)`, with the tabulated CL,
  Vc and VELF; this is equivalent to either half of the printed equations on
  its own and gives a typical fasted AUC0-12,ss of 47 mg.h/L, the reading
  under which the fitted values reproduce the exposure they were fitted to.
  The supplement also lists `Q_CORR = Q/BIO`, but the final model has no `Q`.
* **Albumin effect on Ka not encoded.** The final model has
  `Ka = 0.48 x (ALB/0.93)^8.02 x exp(eta1)`. The reference 0.93 is not serum
  albumin in g/L or g/dL, and the paper reports neither the albumin unit nor a
  cohort summary, so the effect cannot be applied to a measured albumin. The
  model's Ka is the value at the albumin reference. The same group's
  nemonoxacin analysis (`Chen_2023_nemonoxacin`) expressed albumin as the
  measured value divided by the midpoint of the normal range, on which 0.93
  would be a plausible median; Wu 2026 does not say so. Ka shapes only the
  absorption profile: steady-state AUC, the ELF penetration ratio and the
  food effect do not depend on it. The covariate is documented in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **No variance for eta3.** The BIO equation carries `exp(eta3 + kappa)` but
  Table S1 reports only the inter-occasion variance of BIO (0.066). eta3 is
  kept at zero variance (`etalfdepot ~ fixed(0)`).
* **Occasion definition.** The paper does not say how an occasion was
  delimited. Plasma and BAL sampling both followed "the fifth or sixth dose",
  so two occasions are provided (`OCC` 1 and 2), the second repeating the
  first's variance. The simulations above use a single occasion per patient.
  Because the two occasion etas are multiplexed by indicators, rxode2 prints
  `some etas defaulted to non-mu referenced ... etaiov_fdepot_1,
  etaiov_fdepot_2` on each solve. The warning concerns an estimation-time
  optimisation (mu-referencing); simulation is unaffected.
* **Fed bioavailability above 1.** `0.557 x 1.83 = 1.02`. It is kept as
  published; only 2 of the 15 patients were fed.
* **Residual error.** The supplement defines four site-by-matrix proportional
  errors, but Table S1 reports only three: no ELF samples came from Shanghai
  First People's Hospital, so the ELF residual SD (0.001, an estimate at the
  boundary with 99.7% shrinkage) applies to every ELF observation. The main
  text Discussion describes study site as "a random effect"; the supplement
  equations (site-specific residual variances) are followed.
* **Table S1 unit typo.** Table S1 gives the unit of CL as 1/h; the equation
  gives L/h, which is used.
* **Steady-state trough.** The simulated median Cmin of the fasted cohort is
  far below the observed NCA mean of 1.28 mg/L (Table 3), and the model's
  terminal half-life (about 1.4 h, set by the absorption rate) is shorter than
  the NCA half-life of 3.33 h. The NCA was computed on composite sparse
  samples from 15 patients, and the albumin effect (exponent 8.02), which is
  not encoded, produced large between-patient differences in Ka that this
  model can represent only through the Ka variance. Parameters were not
  adjusted.
* **Model-based AUC and PTA not reproduced.** Table 4 reports a model-based
  mean (median) plasma AUC0-12,ss of 71.95 (61.05) mg.h/L, and Figure 4
  implies a median near 68 mg.h/L, against the typical fasted 47 mg.h/L here
  (fed: 87 mg.h/L). Steady-state AUC depends only on dose, BIO and CL, so the
  gap reflects the individual bioavailability estimates and food states of
  the patients the authors simulated, which are not reported.
